candidates.attacker_control: The command list is supplied by the embedding application through NuProcessBuilder(List<String>/String...) (NuProcessBuilder.java:105-113, 142-150). NuProcess's intended use is launching external programs with caller-provided arguments, so in wrapper/converter/CLI-frontend scenarios an untrusted string (e.g., a filename, pattern, or user-supplied parameter) commonly lands in commands[1..n]. No validation or escaping of cmd.exe metacharacters occurs anywhere on the path commands -> prepareProcess -> getCommandLine -> WindowsCreateProcessEscape.quote -> CreateProcessW.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: I derived the MSVC/CRT quoting algorithm from first principles and traced multiple cases (embedded quotes, N- and 2N+1 backslash runs before quotes, trailing backslashes before the closing quote, empty arguments, joining of adjacent arguments). The implemented algorithm in WindowsCreateProcessEscape.java:44-116 is correct for the CRT/CommandLineToArgvW tokenizer, and the code comment at WindowsProcess.java:663-666 (justifying escaping of the executable path) is consistent with that correctness. Therefore the classic 'backslash/quote escaping is broken' hypothesis is NOT supported by the source and is not claimed here. The remaining gap (no cmd.exe metacharacter handling) only materializes when the target is interpreted by cmd.exe; no in-repo demonstration of a .bat/.cmd target or attacker input exists, and I performed no runtime testing.
candidates.impact: Argument/command injection on Windows: a crafted argument can alter the invoked program's argument list, or, when the target is a batch/cmd script, cause arbitrary commands to be executed (file read/write, secondary process execution, etc.) with the privileges of the Java process running NuProcess. Impact depends on the embedding application's trust model; in a privileged service that shells out to batch wrappers with user-influenced parameters this becomes RCE.
candidates.prerequisites: Windows platform; the spawned program must be interpreted by cmd.exe (a .bat/.cmd file, or cmd.exe itself, e.g. 'cmd /c script.bat'), which is a normal use of this library on Windows; the application must place attacker-influenced text into the command list; the caller must not sanitize it beforehand. Plain .exe targets are not affected by cmd.exe parsing.
candidates.root_cause: WindowsProcess.getCommandLine() joins every element of the caller-supplied command list via WindowsCreateProcessEscape.quote() and passes the single resulting string to CreateProcessW (lpApplicationName = NULL), without any cmd.exe-aware escaping or command/argument validation. quote()/mightNeedQuotes() only handle the MSVC/CRT tokenizer (space, tab, double quote, backslash runs), so shell metacharacters that cmd.exe interprets (&, |, ^, <, >, and % / ! expansion) are emitted verbatim. Windows implicitly executes .bat/.cmd targets through cmd.exe /c, so an attacker-influenced argument crosses from data into cmd.exe command syntax.
candidates.title: Windows command-line construction does not neutralize cmd.exe metacharacters when the line is dispatched to cmd.exe (batch/cmd targets)
candidates.trace: NuProcessBuilder.start()/run() (NuProcessBuilder.java:254-274) -> WinProcessFactory.createProcess/runProcess (WinProcessFactory.java:39-52) -> WindowsProcess.start/run -> prepareProcess (WindowsProcess.java:282-309) builds STARTUPINFO and calls NuKernel32.CreateProcessW(null, getCommandLine(commands), ..., bInheritHandles=true, ...) at line 302 -> getCommandLine (652-670) appends each command through WindowsCreateProcessEscape.quote(sb, command) -> quote() (44-116) quotes only if the argument contains space/tab/quote and escapes only backslash runs preceding quotes; characters like '&', '|', '^', '<', '>', '%' pass through unchanged. Windows then resolves the first token and, for .bat/.cmd executables, spawns cmd.exe /c with this line, where the unescaped metacharacters are re-interpreted as command syntax.
candidates.unverified: No runtime/Windows execution was performed (read-only review; no code execution permitted). I could not verify from the repository alone that any caller passes attacker-controlled strings to a .bat/.cmd or cmd.exe target, nor whether cmd.exe would treat the specific constructed fragment as a command in every quoting/expansion edge case (% expansion, delayed expansion, caret handling). The finding is a source-evidence-based lead, not a confirmed exploit.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-88 argument injection leading to CWE-78 OS command injection (Windows)

coverage_summary: Scope: 52 repository-relative files (source_root_files=52; 0 excluded by size/symlink/sensitive-name filters; parity with B0 confirmed). I read all main library sources: NuProcessBuilder/NuProcess/NuProcessHandler/NuAbstractProcessHandler/NuProcessFactory; internal (BasePosixProcess, BaseEventProcessor, IEventProcessor, ReferenceCountedFileDescriptor, LibC, LibJava8, LibJava10, Constants, HexDumpElf); codec (NuAbstractCharsetHandler, NuCharsetDecoder/Encoder and handler interfaces); linux (LinuxProcess, ProcessEpoll, EpollEvent, LibEpoll, LinProcessFactory); osx (OsxProcess, ProcessKqueue, LibKevent, OsxProcessFactory); windows (WindowsProcess, WindowsCreateProcessEscape, ProcessCompletions, NuKernel32, NuWinBase32, NuWinNT, WinProcessFactory); plus examples (NuSchool, OldSchool, SshExample), benchmark sources, and build/CI files (pom.xml, benchmark/pom.xml, .travis.yml, appveyor.yml, shippable.yml, benchmark.sh, README.md, CHANGES.md). P1 relation index reported 52/52 files indexed, 663 symbols, 1255 calls, 1075 edges, 23 navigational facts; the index is navigation-only and every relation used was re-checked against source text. Both a full-file read pass and targeted searches (quote/escape/exec/CreateProcess/SYSCALL/NUL/security) were performed.
limitations: No tests are present in the snapshot (src/test/java referenced by pom.xml is absent), so no regression test or test-name evidence could be inspected.
No code was executed and no target platform (Windows) was exercised; all conclusions are static source reading only, and runtime reachability/exploitability is unproven.
The P1 index is syntactic navigation only (no data-flow, reachability, or semantic resolution); its 'security_call' facts are name-based hints, not findings.

No external advisory/CVE/ground-truth data was consulted (per instructions), so I could not confirm whether this snapshot maps to a publicly tracked issue; the submitted candidate is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

No in-repo caller demonstrates untrusted input reaching a .bat/.cmd target; exploitability depends on the embedding application's usage pattern and on Windows cmd.exe parsing semantics that could not be verified at runtime.
Solaris factory referenced by NuProcessBuilder (com.zaxxer.nuprocess.solaris.SolProcessFactory) has no sources in this snapshot, so that platform path is uninspected.

rejected_leads.lead: WindowsCreateProcessEscape backslash/quote escaping is incorrect (argument injection on Windows)
rejected_leads.reason: Verified from first principles that the algorithm implements the documented MSVC/CRT rules correctly (2N+1 backslashes before a literal quote, 2N before the closing quote, correct empty/whitespace handling); the source comment at WindowsProcess.java:663-666 matches. No source evidence of a quoting bug, so this classic hypothesis is rejected.

rejected_leads.lead: Missing NUL-byte validation in POSIX argument/environment block construction (LinuxProcess.prepareProcess lines 130-191; toEnvironmentBlock lines 213-231), unlike java.lang.ProcessImpl/ProcessEnvironment
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine hardening gap but weak as a vulnerability: NuProcessBuilder builds the env array from a caller-supplied map, so callers already control the execve inputs; no in-repo sink shows attacker control of only a value, and native childproc block-scan behavior could not be verified statically. Not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Windows named pipes created with a NULL security descriptor and opened by name (CreateFile) allow a local attacker to hijack the child's stdin/stdout/stderr
rejected_leads.reason: Pipe names embed a random UUID (WindowsProcess.java:88) and the window between CreateNamedPipeW and CreateFile is a same-thread, microsecond race; no evidence of practical attacker advantage. Not reported.

rejected_leads.lead: CreateProcessW called with lpApplicationName=NULL causes current-directory binary planting on Windows
rejected_leads.reason: Matches java.lang.ProcessImpl behavior and documented Windows search semantics; no repository-specific deviation or reachability evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: Insecure HTTP download of Maven in appveyor.yml (supply chain / MITM)
rejected_leads.reason: CI-only configuration (appveyor.yml:14-17), not shipped library code; low relevance to the library's runtime attack surface.

rejected_leads.lead: Buffer position/limit arithmetic in readStdout/readStderr/writeStdin and the kevent/epoll event loops
rejected_leads.reason: Checked bounds against buffer capacities and OS-reported transferred counts; arithmetic is bounded and consistent with the JDK-derived logic. No out-of-bounds or overflow evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: Insecure benchmark handling of /tmp/random.dat in benchmark.sh/NuProcessBenchmark
rejected_leads.reason: Developer-only benchmark/example artifact; not part of the library's exposed functionality.

summary: Reviewed the NuProcess 2.0.5-SNAPSHOT source snapshot (52 files: library main sources for Windows/POSIX, codec helpers, examples, benchmark, and build/CI config). The code appears to be faithful upstream NuProcess; I found no injected or obvious memory-safety/validation flaw, and I verified from first principles that the WindowsCreateProcessEscape backslash/quote algorithm implements the documented MSVC/CRT argument-quoting rules correctly (literal quotes, trailing backslashes before the closing quote, and argument joining all check out). The strongest single lead is the Windows command-line construction: WindowsProcess.getCommandLine() plus WindowsCreateProcessEscape only neutralize space/tab/quote for the CRT parser and apply no shell-aware escaping or validation, while the resulting line is handed to CreateProcessW with lpApplicationName=NULL. When the target resolves to a .bat/.cmd script (or cmd.exe itself), Windows dispatches the line through cmd.exe /c, where metacharacters such as &, |, ^, !, <, > are interpreted, so an attacker-influenced argument can inject commands/arguments. I submit this as one candidate/lead, not a confirmed vulnerability, and record the verified-correct CRT quoting as counterevidence.
